body: Hi @electricduck, that feels like expected behaviour, if the config directory doesn't exists then it would need to be created. You can try running `mkdir -p ~/.config && touch ~/.config/starship.toml` which should create an empty config file. If you want to change the config location you can use the `STARSHIP_CONFIG` environment variable to change the default location. The [config docs](https://starship.rs/config/) go into this in more detail.
That's what I tried doing. `~/.config` already exists, and I've tried manually creating `~/.config/starship.toml` myself to no avail, to which its not reading anything from it.

Hmm that is very strange, can you try running the following
```
env STARSHIP_LOG=trace starship prompt
```

Weirdly, it does say its parsing the config file, but as you can plainly see, its still using the default prompt.

Ah ok, I know what the problem is. When we released v0.45.0 we made some breaking changes, see [the migration guide](https://starship.rs/migrating-to-0.45.0/), I think if you make the following change it should fix the issue.
```diff
[character]
- symbol = "➜"
+ success_symbol = "[➜](bold green)"
+ error_symbol = "[➜](bold red)"
```
Closing this is I think the issue is resolved, if not please feel free to reopen it.
